"executive_summary": "This study applies Attenuated Total Reflectance Fourier Transform Infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy to monitor the global molecular changes in murine macrophage RAW 264.7 cells upon activation with CpG DNA and lipopolysaccharide (LPS). The authors state that \"Whether CpG ODN-mediated immune activation leads to global molecular changes in cells that are detected by FTIR spectroscopy is currently unknown,\" framing the central knowledge gap. Using ATR-FTIR, they avoided the water-absorption limitation of conventional IR by employing a diamond-ZnSe crystal and direct sample deposition, requiring only a small amount of sample. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) reduced the dimensionality of the spectral data, with PC-1 accounting for 83% of variability and PC-2 for 11%, enabling identification of the sources of variation. Detailed peak analysis revealed that CpG DNA and LPS increase total nucleic acid concentration from the early periods post-activation, with DNA synthesis following RNA synthesis. The RNA-specific peak at 915 cm⁻¹ (ribose vibration) was shown to indicate the activation state of macrophages in early periods post-treatment, allowing detection as early as 10 minutes. Protein concentration increased rapidly initially and leveled off two hours post-activation, as reflected by the amide I (1639 cm⁻¹) and amide II (1540 cm⁻¹) peaks. Both activated groups increased the concentration of fatty acids, triglycerides, and cholesterol, pointing to a shared synthesis pathway and de novo lipogenesis. The study concludes that FTIR spectroscopy can serve as an independent modality to monitor the activation dynamics of murine macrophages. The authors emphasize that this technique provides a broad view of the relative amounts of nucleic acids, lipids, proteins, and other metabolites that are not readily accessible by other techniques, contrasting with the trending omics techniques that yield precise quantitative data on specific molecules. The experimental design used four time points (10 min, 30 min, 2 h, and 6 h) to evaluate the kinetics of induced effects, with five replicates per group. The findings align with prior gene expression studies showing that LPS induces up to 263 genes and that CpG DNA induces short-lived immune activation regulated by synchronized inducers and suppressors. This work demonstrates the utility of FTIR as a non-destructive, rapid, and high-throughput tool for studying cellular responses to stimulatory motifs, which can foster the design of oligodeoxynucleotides (ODNs) for therapeutic uses. The study contributes to understanding the rules governing cellular responses to stimulatory motifs, bridging the gap between bulk analysis and targeted molecular profiling.",

summary.title: Activation of Macrophages by CpG DNA and LPS: an FTIR Spectroscopic Study
summary.authors: Emrulla Spahiu, Senol Dogan, Jörg Schnauß, Mayda Gursel, Feride Severcan
summary.type_of_paper: Experimental study (spectroscopic investigation of macrophage activation)
summary.executive_summary: This study applies Attenuated Total Reflectance Fourier Transform Infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy to monitor the global molecular changes in murine macrophage RAW 264.7 cells upon activation with CpG DNA and lipopolysaccharide (LPS). The authors state that "Whether CpG ODN-mediated immune activation leads to global molecular changes in cells that are detected by FTIR spectroscopy is currently unknown," framing the central knowledge gap. Using ATR-FTIR, they avoided the water-absorption limitation of conventional IR by employing a diamond-ZnSe crystal and direct sample deposition, requiring only a small amount of sample. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) reduced the dimensionality of the spectral data, with PC-1 accounting for 83% of variability and PC-2 for 11%, enabling identification of the sources of variation. Detailed peak analysis revealed that CpG DNA and LPS increase total nucleic acid concentration from the early periods post-activation, with DNA synthesis following RNA synthesis. The RNA-specific peak at 915 cm⁻¹ (ribose vibration) was shown to indicate the activation state of macrophages in early periods post-treatment, allowing detection as early as 10 minutes. Protein concentration increased rapidly initially and leveled off two hours post-activation, as reflected by the amide I (1639 cm⁻¹) and amide II (1540 cm⁻¹) peaks. Both activated groups increased the concentration of fatty acids, triglycerides, and cholesterol, pointing to a shared synthesis pathway and de novo lipogenesis. The study concludes that FTIR spectroscopy can serve as an independent modality to monitor the activation dynamics of murine macrophages. The authors emphasize that this technique provides a broad view of the relative amounts of nucleic acids, lipids, proteins, and other metabolites that are not readily accessible by other techniques, contrasting with the trending omics techniques that yield precise quantitative data on specific molecules. The experimental design used four time points (10 min, 30 min, 2 h, and 6 h) to evaluate the kinetics of induced effects, with five replicates per group. The findings align with prior gene expression studies showing that LPS induces up to 263 genes and that CpG DNA induces short-lived immune activation regulated by synchronized inducers and suppressors. This work demonstrates the utility of FTIR as a non-destructive, rapid, and high-throughput tool for studying cellular responses to stimulatory motifs, which can foster the design of oligodeoxynucleotides (ODNs) for therapeutic uses. The study contributes to understanding the rules governing cellular responses to stimulatory motifs, bridging the gap between bulk analysis and targeted molecular profiling.

The study contributes to understanding the rules governing cellular responses to stimulatory motifs, bridging the gap between bulk analysis and targeted molecular profiling.

Research Context
FTIR spectroscopy is a powerful biomedical tool for non-destructive analysis. A single spectrum reveals alterations in macromolecules. The IR spectrum serves as a fingerprint for metabolites. Water absorbance limits infrared spectroscopy of aqueous systems. ATR-FTIR has multiple applications in hematology. Macrophages are the front line of the immune system. CpG DNA triggers macrophage proliferation and cytokine production. How CpG ODN activation impacts metabolites is unstudied. LPS is a main constituent of gram-negative bacterial cell walls. LPS and CpG share TLR4/TLR-9 signaling pathways. Omics techniques require complex sample preparation.

Research Question And Hypothesis
Whether CpG ODN activation causes detectable global molecular changes. FTIR can monitor macrophage activation dynamics non-invasively. CpG DNA and LPS increase nucleic acid concentration early. DNA synthesis follows RNA synthesis post-activation. The RNA-specific peak indicates early activation state. Protein concentration increases then levels off post-activation. Both stimuli increase fatty acids, triglycerides, and cholesterol. A shared synthesis pathway and de novo lipogenesis occur. PCA identifies the sources of spectral variation. The RNA peak detects activation as early as 10 minutes.

Methodological Details
Cells were murine macrophage-like RAW 264.7 cells. Cells were cultured at 37°C with 5% CO2. Culture medium was DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS. Medium also contained 2 mM L-glutamine. Sub-culturing was done in a 1/10 ratio. Cells were spun at 1000 rpm (208 g) for 10 min. Cell concentration was 2x10^6/mL. Control group was treated with 0.9% PBS. CpG group was treated with 1 µM K3 ODN. LPS group was treated with 0.5 µg/ml LPS. Four time points were used: 10 min, 30 min, 2 h, 6 h. Samples were washed with 15 mL of sterile PBS. Spectrometer was a Perkin-Elmer Spectrum One. ATR unit had a Diamond-ZnSe crystal. Spectra were recorded in the 4000-650 cm^-1 region. Cell samples of 1 µl were dried with N2 flux. Best signal-to-noise used 128 scan number. Spectral resolution was 2 cm^-1. Each group was scanned in three independent scans. Replicates (n=5) were used in data analysis. Savitzky-Golay smoothing used 13 points. Baseline correction was at 3800-2750-1800-900 cm^-1. PCA used Unscrambler 11.0 software. PCA region was 3000-650 cm^-1. Normality was tested with GraphPad Prism 8. Peak assignment used center of weight measurements. Second derivative spectrum was used for side-peak assignment. Concentration studies integrated curves under peaks. Conformational studies used 75% height of peaks.

Procedures And Architectures
A comprehensive spectrum of resting control cells was presented. The spectrum covered the 4000-650 cm^-1 region. The spectrum showed a second derivative. The spectrum contained peaks from lipids, proteins, nucleic acids. Lipid peaks were in the 3000-2800 cm^-1 region. Protein peaks were in the 1700-1600 cm^-1 region. Nucleic acid peaks were at 1238, 1110, and 1085 cm^-1. PCA reduced dimensionality of large data sets. PCA is an unsupervised multivariate data analysis method. Scores Plot showed clusters of similar data. Loadings Plot showed sources of highest variation. PC-1 gave a variability of 83%. PC-2 had a variability of 11%. Loadings Plots showed the 1750-850 cm^-1 region. Nucleic acid peaks showed prominent differences. Symmetric PO2 stretching was at 1085 cm^-1. CpG DNA induced significant changes from 10 min to 6 h. The RNA-specific peak appeared at 915 cm^-1. The RNA peak increased from the first minutes. The RNA increase was maintained until 2 h. Amide I was at 1639 cm^-1 and amide II at 1540 cm^-1. Total protein increased from 10 min to 2 h. The initial protein increase was reduced from 2 h. Triglycerides and cholesterol peaked near 1741 cm^-1. There was a very significant increase during activation. LPS elevated triglycerides and cholesterol after 10 min. Fatty acid concentration increased significantly. The fatty acid peak was at 1400 cm^-1. LPS induces up to 263 genes during stimulation. LPS inhibits DNA synthesis and elicits cell cycle arrest. Activation was defined as early as 41 min after stimulation.

Key Results
PCA PC-1 accounted for 83% of variability. PCA PC-2 accounted for 11% of variability. CpG DNA increased nucleic acid content from 10 min to 6 h. The RNA peak increased from the first minutes. The RNA increase was maintained until 2 h. CpG DNA increased total protein from 10 min to 2 h. Protein increase was reduced from 2 h. LPS increased total protein similarly. Triglycerides and cholesterol increased from the first minutes. LPS elevated triglycerides and cholesterol after 10 min. Fatty acid concentration increased significantly. Both groups increased fatty acids, triglycerides, and cholesterol. DNA synthesis follows RNA synthesis. The RNA peak defines activation at the first minutes. LPS induces up to 263 genes during stimulation. LPS inhibits DNA synthesis and elicits cell cycle arrest. Activation was defined as early as 41 min after stimulation. CpG-induced activation triggers lipogenesis to modulate secretory activity. A shared metabolite links fatty acid and cholesterol synthesis. FTIR provides a broad view of metabolite amounts. The study demonstrates FTIR as an independent modality.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The RNA peak indicates the activation state early. DNA synthesis follows RNA synthesis post-activation. The 2 h period is extensive RNA synthesis. DNA synthesis starts from 6 h after stimulation. LPS is a potent pro-inflammatory and anti-proliferative agent. LPS represses cell cycle-related genes. CpG DNA induced activation was short-lived. Suppressors decline activation after 3 h. Cholesterol is essential for membrane structure and function. A shared pathway links fatty acid and cholesterol synthesis. Lipogenesis modulates secretory activity of ER and Golgi. FTIR provides a broad view of metabolites. FTIR is non-destructive, rapid, and high-throughput. FTIR can monitor activation dynamics of macrophages. Understanding rules fosters ODN design for therapeutic uses. FTIR gives a broad view not accessible by other techniques. The study fills the gap in the big picture of activation. The study provides an aerial view of total protein fate. The study points to the need for future mechanism studies. The study demonstrates FTIR as an independent modality.
